text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Kythera (enterprise: kythera-prod, EU1) p99 latency alert triggered on dedicated-pool-eu1 (SLO: 99th <= 250ms). Spike started at 10:02 UTC, sustained > 3 min. auto-escalation to #incidents and oncall.

maria: paging @owen oncall — you seeing this? metrics look like tail latency for text-gen up ~600-900ms p99; p95 at ~320ms.

own: on it. joining bridge in 2. already looking at recent deploys. @sre-bot can you dump the pool utilization and tenant hot-keys?

sre-bot: pool eu1-dedicated-kythera: GPU util 92%, queue depth spiked from 12->48, avg token rate +210%. Top tenants by qps: kythera-prod(tenant_id: t-kythera) 78%, background-analytics 9%, internal-test 4%. KV cache hit rate dropped from 85%->60% for kythera.

maria: thanks. 2 suspected causes: traffic surge from kythera or cache invalidation after model switch. any recent model rollouts pinned to kythera?

jia: I rolled forward a minor model variant for kythera at 09:58 to 1.2.3-quant. Can roll back if that's the cause.

own: hold on rollback until we confirm. Rolling back might thrash cache more. First: isolate impact, then mitigation.

simone: recommend fast tenant-shielding: move kythera to its own micro-pool (warm spare) to stop noisy-neighboring evictions. We have 2 warm spares in eu1 reserved for reserved customers.

raj: agree. plan: 1) divert new requests from kythera to warm-spare-a (manual routing) 2) throttle kythera concurrency to reduce queue pressure 3) scale up dedicated pool if warm-spare doesn't absorb. 4) if model variant is culprit, prepare rollback.

own: executing step 1 now. command: 
```
redwoodctl route set --pool eu1-warm-spare-a --tenant t-kythera --match "tenant_id==t-kythera" --priority high
```
Applying...

sre-bot: routing change applied, start-time 10:07:12 UTC. New requests should hit eu1-warm-spare-a.

maria: check latency on the warm-spare and original pool. who can tail logs for the evicted requests?

jia: tailing request logs now: seeing many long-running completions for kythera with repeated attention context sizes (~4k tokens). A spike in conversation length from kythera's weekend batch job started at 09:57 UTC.

own: step 2: throttling. setting concurrency cap to 6 for kythera to keep p99 within SLO while we stabilize. command: 
```
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant t-kythera --concurrency 6
```
Applied at 10:08:00 UTC.

sre-bot: after routing + throttle: eu1-dedicated-kythera: queue depth -> 10, GPU util -> 74%. eu1-warm-spare-a p99=280ms (improved), kythera p99 overall now 310ms. p95 back under 250ms.

tara (CS): Kythera support reported timeouts in their dashboard; they asked if this is region-related. Preparing a short note: "We are actively mitigating an elevated latency event for EU1; requests are being routed to a warm spare with minimal disruption."

simone: good. next: runbook check — avoid rolling model variant yet. Cache warming: we can pre-warm KV cache on the warm-spare by replaying recent prefixes for kythera to reduce cold-miss penalty. can trigger replay job.

jia: launching cache-warm replay (job id: replay-4212) targeted to eu1-warm-spare-a. command: 
```
redwoodops replay --tenant t-kythera --pool eu1-warm-spare-a --dataset last-6h --concurrency 4
```
Started 10:12:35 UTC.

sre-bot: replay job progress: 40% after 60s. observed KV hit rate on warm-spare improving from 30% -> 67%.

own: monitoring tail latencies. p99 trending toward 220-260ms. still seeing occasional spikes around 400ms correlated with long prefix sizes.

maria: if spikes persist after warm-spare warmed, we'll consider temporary model quantization bump (more efficient runtime) for kythera — but that needs eng approval due to potential quality change. @raj can you weigh in?

raj: quantization suggestion: switch to 8-bit dynamic profile for kythera-1.2.3 which should reduce p99 by ~30% in our bench. Risk: minor diff in outputs. We can enable as a canary on warm-spare for 5% traffic.

own: hold that as backup. Primary plan: keep routing + throttle + cache warm. If p99 stays < 300ms for 10m we can close the active page and continue observation.

sre-bot: metrics: 10:18 UTC p99=238ms, p95=190ms, queue depth=6, GPU util=66%. Alert auto-mute scheduled for 10:25 if stable.

maria: informing Kythera: Tara, send: "We've routed traffic to a dedicated warm spare and applied temporary concurrency limits. We're monitoring closely; no data loss. We expect restored SLO within minutes."

tara (CS): sent message to Kythera CSM + engineering. They acknowledged and asked for ETA; I gave 20m.

jia: replay job finished 10:22:20 UTC. KV hit rate on warm-spare now 89% for kythera.

own: seeing p99 steady 215-245ms. I'll keep the routing in place for 30m then gradually move traffic back.

simone: add post-incident actions: - investigate why kythera batch job ran against production during peak window - add auto-tenant-shielding rule when single tenant >70% pool qps - evaluate capacity headroom for dedicated pools (target reserve 15%)

raj: also: store metrics snapshot and attach to the incident ticket. I'll prepare a short RCA draft after handoff.

own: handing off to night oncall @simone in 40m. I'll remain reachable if things regress.

maria: recording: incident_id 2026-INC-4212345678. Severity: sev2 (SLO breach, partial impact).

sre-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. last update 10:28:19 UTC.

tara (CS): Kythera message: "Thanks — latency seems improved. We'll continue internal validation and let us know if you need anything"

own: closing active page. moving to watchlist for 2h. Follow-up: postmortem and action items assigned to eng-raj, simone, and jia.

simone: noted. handoff: @simone (night oncall) taking over at 23:00 UTC.

maria: thanks team. good coordination. :thumbsup:
